chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from al-Yaqtini, from Yunus who said:

The Righteous Servant [al-Kadhim] (peace be upon him) said: O Yunus, be lenient towards them, for your words are hard-hitting on them. I said: But they call me a Zindiq [Gnostic/Disbeliever]. He said to me: What will it harm you if you have in your hands a pearl but the people say to you 'it is a stone', and what will it benefit you if you have in your hand a stone but the people say 'it is a pearl'.

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: The Righteous Servant (a title for Imam Musa al-Kadhim)
key_terms.حِصَاةٌ: Stone, symbolizing common or lesser value
key_terms.زَنْدِيقٌ: Zindiq, a term for a Gnostic or someone perceived as a disbeliever/heretic
key_terms.لُؤْلُؤَةٌ: Pearl, symbolizing true value or status
key_terms.يُونُسَ: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, a prominent narrator

ai.seo_question: What is the lesson of the pearl and the stone in the hadith of Imam al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Kashsh al-I'tibār highlights the spiritual resilience required of the righteous amidst societal misunderstanding, a theme central to the Shia concept of *al-ghurba* (strangeness). Imam al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of the pearl and the stone to teach that intrinsic spiritual value (*haqiqa*) remains unchanged regardless of external labels (*zahir*), encouraging Yunus to endure the title of 'Zindiq' with patience as a mark of distinction rather than a defect.

en.ammaar-muslim: 3. [3/284] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh from al-Yaqtini from Yunus who said:

The Righteous Servant [al-Kadhim] عليه السلام said: O Yunus - be more lenient towards them for your words are hard-hitting on them. I said: but they call me Zindiq! He said to me: What will it harm you if you have in your hands a pearl but the people say to you ‘it is a stone’, and what will it benefit you if you have in your hand a stone but the people say ‘it is a pearl’.
